title: From Denial to Purpose — John 21:17
paragraphs: From Denial to Purpose — John 21:17
Here’s a viral-style Facebook post built from John 21:17:
The third question broke him.

Not the nails.
Not the crowd.
Not the fire in the high priest’s courtyard.
This question.
“Do you love Me?” — John 21:17

Peter had already denied Jesus three times.
Three times.
Not once in weakness. Repeatedly. Publicly. Painfully.
And now Jesus asks him three times.

Not to shame him.
To reach the wound.

That’s the kind of Savior we have.
Jesus does not heal us by pretending the failure never happened.
He brings us back to the very place of collapse… and speaks purpose over the ruins.

Peter said, “Lord, You know all things; You know that I love You.”
And Jesus replied, “Feed My sheep.”
Did you catch it?

Jesus did not say,
“Prove yourself first.”
“Earn your way back.”
“Sit in the corner until I trust you again.”
No.

He restored him.
Then recommissioned him.

This is the Gospel.
Your worst moment does not get the final word.
Your denial is real. Your sin is serious. Your tears matter.
But for the one who repents, grace is greater than disgrace.

Peter fell hard.
But Christ’s mercy went deeper.

And maybe that is you right now.
You love Jesus, but you know you have failed Him.
You said things. Hid things. Chose fear. Backed away. Went silent when you should have stood.
But here’s what we miss:

Jesus still comes looking for broken disciples.
Still cooks breakfast for failures.
Still asks heart-searching questions.
Still calls wounded people into holy purpose.

From denial to purpose.
From ashes to assignment.
From shame to shepherding.
Only Jesus can do that.

So come back.
Not to religion.
To Christ.
Repent. Receive His grace. And rise when He calls your name again.

“Do you love Me?”
Then follow Him.
